entities.name: Timer T3502
entities.description: Timer used in 5GMM procedures, with value configurable by network via REGISTRATION ACCEPT or REGISTRATION REJECT messages. Default value used when no value is provided or specific conditions occur.

entities.name: REGISTRATION ACCEPT
entities.description: Message sent by network to UE during registration procedure, which may contain T3502 timer value.

entities.name: REGISTRATION REJECT
entities.description: Message sent by network to UE during initial registration procedure, which may contain T3502 timer value.

entities.name: No timer value specified
entities.description: Condition where REGISTRATION ACCEPT message is received without T3502 value specified.

entities.name: No stored timer value
entities.description: Condition where UE does not have a stored value for T3502 timer.

entities.name: New PLMN registration failure without reject
entities.description: Condition where new PLMN (not in equivalent PLMNs) is entered, initial registration fails, registration attempt counter equals 5, and no REGISTRATION REJECT message was received.

entities.name: Timer deactivated by network
entities.description: Condition where network indicates T3502 timer is deactivated.

entities.name: Mobility and periodic update registration failure
entities.description: Condition where new PLMN (not in equivalent PLMNs) is entered, mobility and periodic update registration procedure fails, and registration attempt counter equals 5.

entities.name: Apply default timer value
entities.description: UE behavior to use default T3502 timer value when specific conditions occur.

relations.description: REGISTRATION ACCEPT message may contain T3502 timer value
REGISTRATION REJECT message may contain T3502 timer value during initial registration
No timer value specified in REGISTRATION ACCEPT establishes use of default value
No stored timer value establishes use of default value
New PLMN registration failure without reject establishes use of default value
Timer deactivation by network establishes use of default value
Mobility and periodic update registration failure establishes use of default value
